title: Dial RPC protocol, version 1
description: Newline-delimited JSON frames of `dial rpc`. Client -> server: `request`. Server -> client: `response` (correlated by id) and `event` (unsolicited). Hand-maintained; tests in crates/dial-app/src/rpc/tests.rs keep its method and event names equal to the implementation. ACP (`dial acp`) uses JSON-RPC 2.0 and is not described here.

id.description: Opaque correlation id echoed in the response; null when absent.

images.description: Image files to attach (native dial rpc only): absolute, `~`, or relative to the workspace root. The active model must accept image input (ready.image_input).

inline_images.description: Base64 image bytes to attach (native dial rpc only), e.g. pasted screenshots.

interactive.description: A person answers this client (native dial rpc only): the engine may then ask interactive questions such as directory-access grants. Scripts leave it false.

oneOf.description: Checkpointed turns of the active session that changed files, newest first. Result: {checkpoints:[{turn,label,files}]}.
Files one checkpointed turn changed, with writers and overlap signals. Result: {turn,label,files:[{path,writers,later_turns,overlap}],skipped}.
Diff that restoring one file would apply, and the review token binding it to the current bytes. Result: {turn,path,diff,token}.

Restores reviewed files of one turn. Every token must still match (else code conflict, nothing written); overlapping files need overlap_confirmed. The restore gets its own checkpoint. Result: {turn,restored}.

Undoes the last user turns like /undo: restores their checkpointed files, then rewinds the conversation keeping the abandoned branch as a summary. Result: {turns,files,rollback_error,dropped,note,rewind_error,cleanup_error,conversation_kept}.

Extension rows shown by /extensions: configured and curated MCP servers and skill packages, read from the saved configuration. Result: {mcp:[row],skills:[row]} where row is {id,title,summary,tags,origin,state,details}.

Run one /extensions action through the overlay's owner: install, import, enable, disable, remove or test an MCP server, Smithery steps, catalog browsing, or installing/removing a skill package. Answered when it finishes; progress arrives as extension_progress events. Actions that change files, run a downloaded command, or remove or disable something need confirm:true. Saved config changes apply on apply_settings. Result: {ok, message, action, saved_scope:'global'|'project'|null, apply_settings, form?, catalog?}; form is {submit, target, title, note, error, fields:[{key,label,hint,required,secret}]} and is answered by sending the intent named by submit. One action runs at a time (busy).

intent.description: An /extensions intent, tagged by op: install_curated_mcp{id}, install_mcp{id,values?}, toggle_mcp{id,enable}, remove_mcp{id}, test_mcp{id}, remove_skill{id}, import_mcp{id}, smithery_install{name}, smithery_key{name,key}, smithery_deploy{name,values}, catalog_browse{tab:'Mcp'|'Skills'|'Tools'|'Hooks',query,page}, install_skill{source}.

oneOf.description: Sign in to the configured remote MCP server, as /mcp login does (protocol 2). Emits auth_url/auth_progress/auth_prompt with provider 'mcp:<server>'; cancel with auth_cancel {provider:'mcp:<server>'}. Answered when the flow ends with {server, message}. The grant applies when the server reconnects: apply_settings {reconnect:true}.
Remove the stored sign-in for an MCP server, cancelling a running one (protocol 2). Result: {server, removed}.
This protocol's JSON Schema (the document in docs/rpc-schema.json), for client code generation. Result: the schema object. Answered by the controller, also during a turn.
Set the session's approval mode, as /approval does. Result: {approval, description}.
The workspace roots, as /dirs shows them. Result: {root, dirs:[path]}. Answered from the published projection, also during a turn.
Add a directory to the workspace and persist it, as /add-dir does. `~`, absolute, or relative to the primary root. Result: {changed, path, dirs}.
Remove an added workspace directory, as /remove-dir does. Result: {changed, path, dirs}.
Rewind the unanswered last prompt and send it again, as /retry does. Result: the same shape as send. Refused (invalid_params) when the last message is not an unanswered prompt.
Unload this session's Dial-managed local model; it reloads on the next request. External endpoints are refused. Result: {restarted:true}.
The session's background (`bg`) jobs. Result: {jobs:[{name, command, status, running, stop_requested, terminal}]}. Answered by the controller, also during a turn.
Stop one background job by name. Result: {name, stopped}.

Reload saved settings (with this process's command-line flags) and apply them to the running session, as the terminal does after a settings change. Approval applies in place; any other change rebuilds the agent around the same session, keeping its conversation, todo, plan mode, cost, model choice, resident model and background processes. Host tools are dropped on a rebuild and must be declared again, parked sessions must be resumed again. Result: {applied:'live'|'rebuild', rebuilt, approval?, host_tools_reset?, reconnected?, tools?, model?, image_input?}. Refused (busy) while workers run.

reconnect.description: Rebuild even when nothing changed and reconnect MCP servers instead of keeping their connections, as /mcp reconnect does (after mcp_login). The result adds reconnected.

code.description: Protocol 2 only. Clients must treat values they do not know as failed.

oneOf.description: Asks the host to run a host-declared tool; answer with host_tool_result using the same call_id.

seq.description: Per-connection event sequence; increases by one per plain-RPC event in stdout order.

session_id.description: Session the engine was serving when the event was produced.

request_id.description: Id of the request whose processing produced the event; null for background work between requests.
